title: The Singing Arc: From Falkenau to the Island in the Lake
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Falkenau and Prague: the Arc Before Argentina

stops.name: Falkenau an der Eger: two dates for one birth
stops.date_confidence: contested. English Wikipedia and the older Argentine reference tradition give 21 February 1909; Spanish and Czech Wikipedia, following recent Czech archival work associated with Milan Ripa and Jan Boukal, give 11 October 1909. The February date orders this file. Neither tradition is resolved here.
stops.campa: A son is born in Falkenau an der Eger, a brown-coal and chemical town on the Ohre in German-speaking Bohemia, in the last decade of Austria-Hungary. The town will change its name twice in his lifetime, to Falknov nad Ohri when Czechoslovakia takes it in 1918 and to Sokolov in 1948, by which year he is on the other side of the Atlantic and calling himself an Austrian. Even the day comes doubled. The Argentine and English books say the twenty-first of February; the Czech archives, worked over since 2021, say the eleventh of October.
suggested_refs: Milan Ripa, Ronald Richter: Termojaderna fuze, prvni na svete, Sokolov 1936 (Sokolov Museum, 2021)
The Charles University doctorate registers for 1931-1936, cited by Czech archival scholarship

stops.name: Prague: the German University in the Karolinum
stops.date_confidence: inferred. The sources reached give only that he graduated from the Natural Sciences Faculty of the German University in Prague in 1935; the start of his studies is nowhere dated, and 1930 is a placeholder to order the segment.
stops.campa: He enrolls in the Natural Sciences Faculty of the German-language half of Charles University, divided from its Czech half since 1882, teaching physics in a city where three languages argue on the same street. He works as an assistant while still a student. Among his contemporaries is Kurt Sitte, who remembers the department, Furth's experimental physics, and the young man from Falkenau, already interested in what heat does to matter once there is enough of it.
stops.quote: cuando yo me desempeñaba como asistente del profesor Furth en el Departamento de Física Experimental
stops.quote_source: Kurt Sitte, on the German University physics department in Prague, quoted in Spanish Wikipedia, 'Ronald Richter'
suggested_refs: The Karolinum and the Natural Sciences Faculty of the German University in Prague, 1928-1938

stops.name: Prague: the doctorate that may or may not exist
stops.date_confidence: graduation in 1935 is attested by both English and Spanish Wikipedia; the day and month are placeholders. Whether a doctorate was conferred is contested: one tradition holds the thesis was refused because he read his own results as delta rays, another cites the university's doctorate register. The register page was not inspected for this file.
stops.campa: He finishes in 1935, and here the paper trail forks. One account, the one Argentina will later use against him, says no degree was given: he had read his results as evidence of delta rays and been told he was wrong. The other, drawn from the doctorate register of the German university, says the degree in natural sciences was conferred and entered in the book. The register page has not been inspected for this file, and both traditions survive intact. For the rest of his life the presidents and the newspapers call him Doctor.
suggested_refs: The doctorate register of the German University in Prague, 1931-1936

stops.name: Falkenau: the singing arc at the chemical works
stops.date_confidence: attested by Czech sources. Czech Wikipedia and Milan Ripa's 2021 Sokolov monograph both fix the experiments at the Falknov nad Ohri chemical works, now Synthomer Sokolov, in 1936, and Ripa describes them as the first attempts at fusion in a plasma made anywhere. The Czech-language originals were not read for this file. The day and month order the segment.
stops.campa: He goes home to work at the chemical works and begins the experiments that will govern the rest of his life: a high-current electric arc, deuterium injected into it, a Geiger counter watching what comes out. The arc is a nineteenth-century object, a thing that hisses and sings between two carbon rods, and he is asking it for the temperatures the sun keeps. Nothing comes of it in Bohemia. Eighty-five years later a Czech physicist will argue in a book that these were the earliest attempts at plasma fusion made anywhere in the world.
suggested_refs: The Falknov nad Ohri chemical works, now Synthomer Sokolov
Milan Ripa, Ronald Richter: Termojaderna fuze, prvni na svete, Sokolov 1936 (2021)
sources: karlovarska.drbna.cz, 'Prvni pokusy s termojadernou fuzi probehly v Sokolove'

stops.name: Berlin: the years Germany does not document
stops.date_confidence: placeholder date and placeholder coordinates. Spanish Wikipedia places him in Germany between 1939 and 1943; no city, laboratory, employer or rank could be confirmed in any source reached. Berlin stands here for German wartime industry in general and is not a documented address.
stops.campa: The war years are a hole in his biography. He is in Germany, working; the names that circle him afterwards are Manfred von Ardenne, Max Steenbeck, Kurt Tank, but no source reached for this file puts him in a named building on a named payroll. In Argentina he will be presented as a physicist out of the German nuclear effort, and by his enemies as a man who was never anywhere near it. There is a reported six months on explosives development and a run of commercial contracts. That is the whole of the record.
suggested_refs: The postwar recruitment of German technical personnel by Argentina, 1946-1948

stops.name: Paris: looking for a buyer
stops.date_confidence: inferred. English Wikipedia says only that after his German work he travelled to England and France; no dates, cities or contacts are given. Paris and the year 1946 order the segment and are not documented.
stops.campa: Postwar Europe is full of men with a technical idea and no state left to sell it to. Richter crosses into France and England carrying his arc, his deuterium, and a proposal that grows larger each time he explains it: first heat, then power, then propulsion. The sources record the movement and nothing else. No laboratory takes him on and no ministry answers; no contact, employer or address is named in anything reached for this file, which holds a direction of travel and not one transaction. He is thirty-seven.
suggested_refs: The market in displaced German and Austrian technical specialists, 1945-1948

stops.name: London: the proposal to Kurt Tank
stops.date_confidence: traditional. Spanish Wikipedia places the meeting with Kurt Tank in England and gives no date; English Wikipedia dates the resulting recommendation to Argentina to 1947. The venue within London is unrecorded and the city-centre pin is a placeholder, as is the month.
stops.campa: In London he meets Kurt Tank, designer of the Focke-Wulf 190, who is himself in the market for a country. Richter proposes nuclear propulsion for aircraft. Tank is not a physicist and has no means of testing the claim, but he has just accepted an offer from Buenos Aires and he has the ear of the men making it. Argentina at this moment owns no reactor and no accelerator, and its universities employ nobody who works in nuclear physics. Tank carries the name south with him.
suggested_refs: Kurt Tank's contract with the Instituto Aerotecnico, Cordoba, from late 1946

stops.name: Puerto Nuevo, Buenos Aires: the arrival
stops.date_confidence: date attested by English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project'. The dock is a placeholder: Puerto Nuevo was the city's passenger port of the period, but no source reached names his point of entry. Spanish Wikipedia's claim that he was naturalised Argentine in September 1946 sits unresolved against this 1948 arrival.
stops.campa: He lands in Buenos Aires on the sixteenth of August, 1948. Argentina that year is rich on wheat and certain it is about to become a world power. No passenger record has been examined for this file and the dock is a guess. The story that follows him ever afterwards, that he entered the country under the alias Doctor Pedro Matthies, belongs to another man: Kurt Tank had been using that name in Cordoba since late 1946, and repetition has folded the two of them together. Richter arrives under his own name.
suggested_refs: Passenger records of Puerto Nuevo, Buenos Aires, August 1948

stops.name: Casa Rosada: presented to Peron
stops.date_confidence: attested by English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', which gives 24 August 1948 for the introduction. The building is the customary site of such presentations and the pin is the canonical Casa Rosada pin used across the corpus; no source reached names the room.
stops.campa: Kurt Tank brings him to Juan Peron. Richter explains fusion: two light nuclei, fuel that costs nothing, temperatures no furnace has ever held, and energy without the six billion dollars the American route would cost. Peron will say afterwards that within half an hour he felt he understood nuclear physics, and he means it as praise. No Argentine physicist is in the room, and none will be consulted. Eva Peron watches her husband come away from the interview lit up.
stops.quote_source: Eva Peron on Richter, quoted in Alicia Dujovne Ortiz, Eva Peron (1996), as reproduced in English Wikipedia, 'Ronald Richter'
suggested_refs: Peron's own account of the first Richter interview, in his later statements on the atomic program

stops.name: Cordoba, Instituto Aerotecnico: the first laboratory
stops.date_confidence: inferred within an attested period. Spanish Wikipedia places his first Argentine facilities at the Instituto Aerotecnico in Cordoba across 1948-1949; the month is a placeholder. Coordinates are those of the Fabrica Argentina de Aviones site.
stops.campa: His first Argentine laboratory is a corner of Tank's aviation institute at Cordoba, where the Pulqui jet fighters are being built by German engineers on Argentine money. He asks for equipment and gets it. He asks for secrecy and gets that too. He is working inside another man's program, in a plant built for airframes, and the arrangement satisfies nobody: the aeronautical people want their machine shop back, and Richter wants a site where no one can look over the fence at all.
suggested_refs: The Instituto Aerotecnico, Cordoba, and the Pulqui program under Kurt Tank

stops.name: Cordoba: the fire
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the event, imprecise as to date. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', gives only that in early 1949 a fire destroyed some of the equipment. The day and month order the segment. The Spanish-language article on the project contains no mention of a fire, and the sabotage claim is Richter's own allegation, not a finding.
stops.campa: In the first weeks of 1949 a fire goes through his equipment at Cordoba. No day is recorded for it anywhere. Richter calls it sabotage, and no proof of sabotage is produced then or afterwards; the fire is equally consistent with a laboratory full of high current and volatile gas, run in a hurry by a man with no colleague to slow him down. The Spanish-language account of the project does not mention a fire at all. What he asks for next is not replacement equipment but an island.
suggested_refs: The 1949 Cordoba laboratory fire and Richter's sabotage allegation

stops.name: Vienna: Lise Meitner is not persuaded
stops.date_confidence: attested as anecdote, undated as to day. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', reports Meitner recalling a meeting in Vienna with a strange Austrian holding an Argentine visa, and dates the encounter to Richter's early-1949 tour. The month orders the segment. The recollection is retrospective testimony, not a laboratory record.
stops.campa: Somewhere in Vienna he demonstrates his device to Lise Meitner, who thirty years earlier did the arithmetic that turned nuclear fission into a fact and was left off the prize for it. She watches. She judges what she has been shown to be a chemical effect rather than a thermonuclear one, and she says so afterwards. It is the earliest competent judgement anyone renders on the apparatus, three years before Argentina asks for one, and nothing is written down at the time. What survives is her recollection of a strange Austrian with an Argentine visa.
suggested_refs: Lise Meitner's recollection of the Vienna demonstration, reported in the Huemul literature

stops.name: Ottawa: the tour that was also a threat
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the tour, placeholder as to place. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', records that when support was not immediately forthcoming Richter went on a tour, visiting Canada and perhaps the United States and Europe as well, in early 1949. No Canadian city is named; Ottawa is a placeholder and so is the month.
stops.campa: Argentine support does not arrive immediately after the fire, so Richter travels. Canada certainly, the United States and Europe possibly; the sources are vague in a way that serves the purpose, because the purpose is to be seen leaving. A man with a fusion project who is calling on other governments is a man who might hand it to one of them. He is back in Argentina within months and the money is found. Nothing in the record says he ever received an offer abroad.
suggested_refs: The 1949 foreign tour and its effect on Argentine funding decisions

stops.name: Isla Huemul: the island is chosen
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year. English and Spanish Wikipedia both date the start of construction on Isla Huemul to 1949; the month is a placeholder within that year. Coordinates from Spanish Wikipedia, 'Isla Huemul' (41 06 23 S, 71 23 42 O).
stops.campa: Colonel Enrique Gonzalez picks the island: rock and cypress in Lago Nahuel Huapi, some eight kilometres out from Bariloche, reachable only by boat, with cold fresh water on every side and a shoreline the army can watch entire. The lake does the work a fence would otherwise have to do, and after Cordoba that is the whole of the requirement. Construction begins in the winter of 1949, under the secrecy the fire has justified: laboratories, workshops, houses, a dock, roads cut through the trees, a boat that goes back and forth to a shore where nothing is explained.
suggested_refs: Colonel Enrique P. Gonzalez and the selection of the Huemul site, 1949

stops.name: San Carlos de Bariloche: the town below the island
stops.date_confidence: inferred. His passage through Bariloche follows from the island's geography, since Isla Huemul is reached only by boat from the mainland shore, but no source reached documents a specific visit or a residence in the town. The pin is the canonical Bariloche pin used elsewhere in the corpus. The date orders the segment.
stops.campa: Everything the island eats comes through Bariloche: cement, transformers, carbon rods, lathes, deuterium, men. The town is a small alpine-styled place of chocolate shops and Swiss-German masonry at the foot of the Andes, and it watches trucks unload onto boats bound for a place it is not permitted to name. Within six years the same lakeshore will hold the physics institute founded so that the country never again has to take one man's word for a result. The rumours arrive early and stay: an atomic bomb, a German laboratory, the President's secret.
suggested_refs: The Bariloche lakefront as supply point for the Huemul works, 1949-1952
The physics institute founded at Bariloche in 1955, renamed Instituto Balseiro in 1962

stops.name: Isla Huemul: Richter moves onto the island
stops.date_confidence: traditional. The March 1950 relocation date is carried from the dossier and was not found in any source fetched for this file; construction from 1949 and his direction of the site through 1952 are both attested. The month orders the segment.
stops.campa: He moves out to the island to direct the work himself, and begins to build and unbuild. Plans change weekly. Walls go up and come down again. He runs the site as a single mind with unlimited credit, corresponding directly with the President over the heads of the officers nominally in charge, and those officers learn quickly that a complaint about Richter is a complaint about Peron. For the whole history of the project there is no second physicist on the island.
suggested_refs: The Huemul works: laboratories, dock, workshops and residences, 1949-1952

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the commission built around one man
stops.date_confidence: attested. Decree No. 10,936 of 31 May 1950 created the Comision Nacional de Energia Atomica, per English Wikipedia's article on the CNEA, and Richter was among its initial members. The pin is the canonical Buenos Aires pin used across the corpus; the decree's signing place is not separately documented here.
stops.campa: Peron creates the Comision Nacional de Energia Atomica by decree on the thirty-first of May, and names to its founding membership the man whose island it exists to fund. The country now has a national atomic energy commission with no reactor and no accelerator, and not one verified experiment behind it; its principal asset is a claim made by a single person on a lake in Patagonia. The commission is still there three quarters of a century later, running the reactors Argentina eventually built. The decree is numbered 10,936.
suggested_refs: Decree No. 10,936 of 31 May 1950 establishing the CNEA
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Comision Nacional de Energia Atomica'

stops.name: Isla Huemul: Laboratorio 1
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The physical description of the reactor building reaches this file through the dossier's synthesis of press reporting on the ruins, chiefly a WIRED long-form piece that could not be fetched this session. Dimensions, wall thickness and the demolition order are unverified. The date orders the segment.
stops.campa: The reactor building rises as a concrete cylinder some twelve metres across, with walls reported at up to four metres thick, a bunker for an experiment that has not worked once. It is built without adequate access to its own interior, so holes are later bored through the walls to reach what is inside. Then Richter finds a crack in it, declares the structure fatally compromised, and orders it pulled down, the concrete not yet a year cured. No source reached for this file describes the crack.
suggested_refs: The concrete reactor shell on Isla Huemul, standing in ruin since 1952
sources: Dossier synthesis of press reporting on the Huemul ruins (WIRED, 2011), not independently fetched

stops.name: Isla Huemul: fourteen metres down, then filled in
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The buried-chamber excavation and the fourteen-metre figure come from the dossier's account of press reporting on the site; the depth could not be independently confirmed for this file. The date orders the segment.
stops.campa: A redesign calls for the reaction chamber to sit deep in rock. Crews cut some fourteen metres down into the island. Then the design changes again, the shaft is filled with concrete, and the island keeps the shape of a hole dug for a reason that lasted a season. The state pays for the digging and then for the filling, and the pair of operations is cited ever afterwards in the accounting of what the money bought. Both figures reach this file through press reporting on the ruins rather than through any account book.
suggested_refs: The filled excavation on Isla Huemul, cited in the cost accounting of the project
sources: Dossier synthesis of press reporting on the Huemul ruins, not independently fetched

stops.name: Isla Huemul: the sixteenth of February
stops.date_confidence: attested as the date Richter claimed. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', gives 16 February 1951 as the run he interpreted as a controlled thermonuclear reaction. That he made the claim is well attested by everything that follows; that the reaction occurred is precisely what the 1952 commissions disproved.
stops.campa: He fires the arc and reads the plates. The spectral lines are broadened, and broadening means motion, and motion of that width means temperature, and temperature at that height means fusion. Nobody else on the island reads the plate, and nobody off it is ever shown one. Whatever else is true of the man, this is the moment he believes it, and the announcement and the medal and the forty years of insisting all come out of it. He writes it down as a controlled thermonuclear reaction on a technical scale.
suggested_refs: The spectrographic plates of 16 February 1951, never independently examined

stops.name: Isla Huemul: the tilted plate
stops.date_confidence: attested as to date, secondhand as to content. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', reports the technician's warning of 23 February 1951 that the line broadening could come from a tilted photographic plate. No transcript or named technician was located for this file.
stops.campa: A technician comes to him a week later with a mundane objection: a photographic plate sitting at an angle will smear a spectral line exactly the way a hot plasma will, and one repetition of the run would settle which it was. Richter does not repeat the run. He redesigns the apparatus instead, and the configuration that produced the only result he ever claimed ceases to exist. Whether the broadening came from a plasma or from a plate at an angle is now a question with nothing left to test it against.
suggested_refs: The measurement-artefact objection of 23 February 1951

stops.name: Casa Rosada: Peron announces a sun
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', dates Peron's announcement of controlled thermonuclear reactions on a technical scale to 24 March 1951. The pin is the canonical Casa Rosada pin used across the corpus. The quoted words are Richter's, reported publicly by Peron in early 1951, and are frequently misattributed to Peron himself.
stops.campa: Peron tells the world from the Casa Rosada that on the sixteenth of February, on Argentine soil, controlled thermonuclear reactions were obtained on a technical scale. Not a bomb: energy. He says it will one day reach households in containers the size of a milk bottle. No paper has been published, and no physicist outside the island has seen the apparatus. The announcement lands days before an inter-American conference and in the middle of a quarrel with Washington, and every wire service on earth carries it.
stops.quote: podía iniciar los trabajos atómicos por el procedimiento que siguen los norteamericanos, pero que para eso necesitaríamos unos seis mil millones de dólares
stops.quote_source: Ronald Richter to Juan Peron, reported publicly by Peron in early 1951; Infobae, 'Los suenos atomicos de Juan Domingo Peron' (2021)
suggested_refs: Wire-service coverage of the Argentine fusion announcement, 25 March 1951
ITER, 'Proyecto Huemul: the prank that started it all', on Lyman Spitzer's response to the announcement and the origin of the stellarator
sources: Infobae, 'Los suenos atomicos de Juan Domingo Peron' (2021)

stops.name: Buenos Aires: ten thousand words
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', places the press conference on the day after the announcement, that is 25 March 1951, and names it the 10,000 word interview. Sources circulating 28 March are three days out. No source reached names the venue; the pin is the canonical Buenos Aires pin.
stops.campa: The day after the announcement Richter faces the press for hours. He denies that Argentina is building an atomic bomb or a hydrogen bomb. He describes power stations, cheap fuel, an energy supply for a continent. He says he understands how a hydrogen bomb would be made and that the President has forbidden him to work on one. He answers every question at length, and not one number in the answers is one another laboratory could check. The Argentine press calls it the ten thousand word interview.
suggested_refs: Argentine press transcripts of the 25 March 1951 Richter conference

stops.name: Casa Rosada: the gold medal
stops.date_confidence: attested as to date. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', dates the award of the gold Medalla Peronista to 7 April 1951. The location of the ceremony is not named in any source reached; the canonical Casa Rosada pin stands for the presidency.
stops.campa: Two weeks after the announcement Peron hangs the gold Medalla Peronista on him. It is the highest decoration the movement gives, and it is given for an experiment that one technician has already questioned and that no outside person has examined. Richter accepts it. Thirty-three years later, in a suburban house with the shutters coming off, he will tell a journalist that he sent the medal back, along with the honorary title the university gave him. No record of either return has been found in any archive reached.
suggested_refs: The gold Medalla Peronista and its conferral of 7 April 1951

stops.name: Universidad de Buenos Aires: the doctorate nobody examined
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The honorary doctorate is carried from the dossier and was not located in any source fetched, including the Spanish Wikipedia article on the university, which supplied only the Rectorado address and coordinates. The month is a placeholder within 1951.
stops.campa: The University of Buenos Aires confers an honorary doctorate on him, at what appears to be executive request, without any faculty of the university examining the work. Argentine physics understands exactly what this is. Juan Roederer, then a young physicist in the country, will write half a century later that the profession was unanimous and silent at the same time. In a country with perhaps a few dozen people competent to judge the claim, not one is on the island and not one is asked. The ceremony proceeds.
stops.quote: Not one real Argentine physicist was participating in the Huemul project, and not one in the entire country believed in the truth of Peron's announcement.
stops.quote_source: Juan G. Roederer, 'Early Cosmic-Ray Research in Argentina', Physics Today, January 2003, as reproduced in English Wikipedia, 'Ronald Richter'
suggested_refs: The Rectorado of the Universidad de Buenos Aires, Viamonte 430
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Universidad de Buenos Aires' (address only)
Dossier synthesis, for the honorary doctorate itself

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the answer to Thirring
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the exchange, corrected as to title. Hans Thirring's skeptical assessment appeared in United Nations World in May 1951 and Richter's signed reply in July 1951, titled 'Argentina Has No Atomic Bomb', verified through the citation list of James Mahaffey's Atomic Adventures. Neither original text was read for this file; the date is an issue month, not a day. The Teller remark quoted here is from a 2003 exchange, half a century later.
stops.campa: The Viennese physicist Hans Thirring puts the odds at ninety-nine to one that the Argentine achievement was imagined rather than performed, in print, in an international magazine. Richter answers over his own signature in the same magazine two months later. It is the only occasion on which he defends himself in the ordinary open forum of the profession, and what he defends himself against is the charge of building a weapon, which nobody outside Argentina had made. The title of the reply is Argentina Has No Atomic Bomb.
stops.quote: Reading one line one has to think he's a genius. Reading the next line, one realizes he's crazy.
stops.quote_source: Edward Teller on reading Richter, cited in the 2003 Physics Today exchange and quoted by ITER, 'Proyecto Huemul: the prank that started it all'
suggested_refs: Hans Thirring in United Nations World, May 1951
Ronald Richter, 'Argentina Has No Atomic Bomb', United Nations World, July 1951
sources: James A. Mahaffey, Atomic Adventures (citation list, via Open Library full-text search)
iter.org, 'Proyecto Huemul: the prank that started it all'

stops.name: Isla Huemul: the protector resigns
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the fact, unlocated as to place. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', records that Gonzalez told Peron in February 1952 that either Richter departed or he would, and that Peron accepted the resignation and replaced him with Navy Captain Pedro Iraolagoitia, who also protested and pressed for an investigation. The scene's location is not recorded; the island pin stands for the project, and the day orders the segment.
stops.campa: Colonel Gonzalez, who chose the island and defended the project for three years, tells Peron that one of the two of them has to go, and Peron takes the resignation. Richter has lost the only man in the government whose own career depended on his being right. The replacement, Captain Pedro Iraolagoitia of the navy, arrives, looks at the accounts and at the apparatus, and starts pressing the President for a technical inspection. Three years of unaudited spending sit in the ledgers he has just inherited.
suggested_refs: Colonel Enrique P. Gonzalez's resignation, February 1952

stops.name: Isla Huemul: five men come to look
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', dates the inspection to 5-8 September 1952 and records Balseiro's urgent recall from England. Spanish Wikipedia gives the membership as Jose Antonio Balseiro, Mario Bancora, Manuel Beninson, Pedro Bussolini and Otto Gamba, assigning no ranks; the English article also places Iraolagoitia with the team. The dossier's 'Juan Bussolini' is unsourced and the Spanish article's 'Pedro' is preferred.
stops.campa: The commission lands on the fifth of September: Jose Antonio Balseiro, recalled urgently from England, the engineers Mario Bancora and Otto Gamba, Manuel Beninson, and the Jesuit physicist Bussolini. They ask Richter to run the apparatus. They ask for the detector readings with the nuclear fuel in place and with it removed. The readings come back the same. Balseiro works through the collision arithmetic for the lithium and finds that under the conditions of operation the control Richter describes is not possible at all.
stops.quote: El resultado obtenido es, pues, que el enorme número de choques sufridos por el átomo de Li, en las condiciones que se opera, imposibilita la realización de cualquier dispositivo de contralor basado en el principio mencionado por el doctor Richter.
stops.quote_source: Jose Antonio Balseiro, Informe de la Comision Tecnica sobre el Proyecto Huemul, September 1952, quoted in Spanish Wikipedia, 'Proyecto Huemul'
suggested_refs: The technical commission reports of September 1952, CNEA archive

stops.name: Isla Huemul: the singing arc
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the finding, imprecise as to the day. The inspection ran 5-8 September 1952 per English Wikipedia; the day within it on which Bancora identified the device is not recorded, and the closing date of the visit is used here.
stops.campa: Mario Bancora looks into the heart of the machine and recognises it. It is a singing arc, the device William Duddell built in London around 1900 to make an electric arc hum a tune, a laboratory curiosity fifty years old. The commission's finding is not that he cheated at physics; it is that his apparatus is a demonstration piece from the previous century, run at enormous current and asked for a star. He has fed it lithium and deuterium and photographed its light.
stops.quote: El dispositivo usado por el Dr. Richter, es el arco cantante descubierto por Dudell hace unos 50 años.
stops.quote_source: Mario Bancora, report of the 1952 Technical Commission on the Huemul project, quoted in Spanish Wikipedia, 'Proyecto Huemul' (spelling of Duddell as in the source)
suggested_refs: William Duddell's singing arc, London, c.1900

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the reports go in
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', dates the delivery of the negative technical reports to 15 September 1952. The canonical Buenos Aires pin is used; no source reached names where the reports were handed over.
stops.campa: Ten days after landing on the island the commission delivers its reports. They find that the theoretical concepts lack the foundations required to permit any hope of a sustained and controlled thermonuclear reaction; that the apparatus cannot reach the temperatures or reaction probabilities the claim requires; that the detectors answer the same with fuel and without; and that the method of operation fails the elementary standards of experimental control. Peron now has the answer he asked for. The reports are dated the fifteenth of September 1952.
stops.quote: Los conceptos teóricos sumados por el Doctor Richter carecen de los fundamentos necesarios para permitir que se abrigue alguna esperanza de una realización exitosa de sus propósitos tendientes a lograr una reacción termonuclear mantenida y controlada.
stops.quote_source: Jose Antonio Balseiro, technical assessment, September 1952, quoted in Infobae, 'Los suenos atomicos de Juan Domingo Peron' (2021)
suggested_refs: Balseiro and Bancora's reports of 15 September 1952
sources: Infobae, 'Los suenos atomicos de Juan Domingo Peron' (2021)

stops.name: Buenos Aires: Gans and Rodriguez read the rebuttal
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the review, unattested as to date. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', records that the government appointed Richard Gans and Antonio Rodriguez to review the first report and Richter's response, and that they endorsed the findings and judged the response inadequate. The precise date of 16 October 1952 carried by the dossier appears in no source fetched for this file; the month orders the segment.
stops.campa: Richter writes a rebuttal, at length, as he answers everything. The government appoints two further physicists, Richard Gans and Antonio Rodriguez, to read it against the commission's reports. Neither man has been on the island and neither is sent there. They are not asked to repeat the experiment; they are asked whether his answer to being told it failed holds up. Work continues on the island for another five weeks after they report, because nobody has yet told Richter to stop. Gans and Rodriguez endorse the commission on every point.
suggested_refs: The Gans and Rodriguez review of the Richter rebuttal, autumn 1952

stops.name: Isla Huemul: the island is taken
stops.date_confidence: attested. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', dates the military occupation of the island, carried out while Richter was in Buenos Aires, to 22 November 1952. Spanish Wikipedia confirms the project's closure that year without giving the day.
stops.campa: Richter is in Buenos Aires when the troops go across the water. The project is declared a failure and closed; he is forty-three, and he has spent four years on this lake, and he will never see it again. There is no trial and no published conviction, only a technical finding, an administrative order, and a set of concrete shells on a lake that nobody now has a reason to cross. What the soldiers find is equipment disconnected, instruments that do not function, buildings half built and half demolished.
suggested_refs: The military occupation of Isla Huemul, 22 November 1952

stops.name: Buenos Aires: three years of not being allowed to leave
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The restricted residence between the project's closure and Peron's overthrow is carried from the dossier and was not located in any source fetched for this file. The address is unknown, the canonical Buenos Aires pin is a placeholder, and the date orders the segment.
stops.campa: For three years he lives in the Buenos Aires area under something between close supervision and house arrest. Peron is reported to have offered to help him travel abroad, in language that could be read as courtesy or as an instruction. He does not go. The government that decorated him cannot prosecute him without prosecuting itself, and cannot release him to talk to foreign newspapers either. So it keeps him, quietly, at an address the record does not give.
suggested_refs: Richter's status between November 1952 and September 1955
sources: Dossier synthesis, not independently located in any fetched source

stops.name: Monte Grande: the chalet at Almirante Brown and Berasain
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year and address. Dataconurbano.net records that he bought a chalet in Monte Grande in 1954 at the corner of Almirante Brown and Berasain; the corner is corroborated by elcordillerano.com.ar, which describes the unfinished stone facade and deteriorated shutters seen by a visitor in 1984. The month is a placeholder. Coordinates are those of Monte Grande.
stops.campa: He buys a chalet on a corner in Monte Grande, south of the capital: a stone facade never finished, shutters that will spend thirty years coming apart. He lives there with his wife Ilse for the rest of his life. The neighbours know he had something to do with the atom and with Peron, and they are not sure whether that made him a genius or a swindler. Within a few years they have settled on a name for him and they keep it to the end. El aleman loco. The crazy German.
suggested_refs: The house at Almirante Brown and Berasain, Monte Grande
sources: dataconurbano.net, 'Ronald Richter, un vecino de Monte Grande que engano a Peron'

stops.name: Buenos Aires: arrested on the night of the fourth of October
stops.date_confidence: attested as to event, carried from the dossier as to the exact night. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', records that after the Revolucion Libertadora the new government investigated Richter over unaccounted project funds and arrested him; the date of 4 October 1955 and the night-time detail were not independently relocated in a fetched source. The address is unknown and the canonical Buenos Aires pin is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Peron falls in September. In October the new government comes for Richter and asks him where the money went. The figure produced is around sixty-two and a half million pesos, some fifteen million dollars of the day, and larger numbers circulate that cannot be compared across peso vintages. The state has established that the physics was wrong; it never separately establishes that the man was a thief. He is held briefly and released, and no conviction or civil judgment against him has been found in any source reached.
suggested_refs: The Revolucion Libertadora investigations into Huemul expenditure, 1955-1956
sources: Dossier chronology, for the arrest date

stops.name: Tripoli: the Libyan rumour
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, with a placeholder date. English Wikipedia, 'Ronald Richter', reports only periods of time abroad including some time in Libya, with no dates, employer or city. The frequently repeated claim that he worked for Muammar Gaddafi is chronologically weak, since Gaddafi took power only in 1969. The pin is the canonical Tripoli pin used elsewhere in the corpus.
stops.campa: After his release he travels, and one of the places the record puts him is Libya. There is no date attached, no employer, no project and no document. The rumour is durable because it has the shape people expect of him: the discredited nuclear man selling himself to a desert government with oil money. What can actually be said is that he went abroad in the years after 1955, that Libya is named among the places, and that everything past that sentence is somebody's inference.
suggested_refs: The reported Libyan residence, undated in every source consulted

stops.name: Monte Grande: Mariscotti at the table
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the interviews, imprecise as to date. English Wikipedia, 'Huemul Project', records that Mario Mariscotti extensively interviewed him for his account, and the book El Secreto Atomico de Huemul appeared in 1985. The interview years are given only as the 1970s and 1980s, and the date here orders the segment. The psychological reading of the man is the dossier's synthesis, not a stated finding.
stops.campa: The physicist Mario Mariscotti finds him in the suburbs and begins the long run of interviews that will become El Secreto Atomico de Huemul, still the standard account of the whole affair. Mariscotti comes away reading him as a man who deceived himself before he deceived anybody else. Richter talks and talks, going through the plates, the arc, the lithium, the conspiracy, the men who could not follow him. He has never for one day stopped believing he was right.
stops.quote: While in a state of delirious enthusiasm [Peron] said [just] anything ... and ventured to prognosticate that I would obtain for him bottled electric energy.
stops.quote_source: Ronald Richter, recollection quoted in Hugo Gambini, Historia del peronismo, vol. 1 (1999), p. 398, as reproduced in English Wikipedia, 'Ronald Richter'
suggested_refs: Mario Mariscotti, El Secreto Atomico de Huemul: cronica del origen de la energia atomica en la Argentina (1985)
sources: archive.org, El Secreto Atomico de Huemul (1985)

stops.name: Isla Huemul: the island handed back
stops.date_confidence: attested. Magicasruinas.com.ar records the military's return of the island to Rio Negro province on 18 August 1984 and quotes Mariscotti on the state of the buildings. That source gives the island as 200 hectares while Spanish Wikipedia gives 74; the conflict is not resolved. Richter was not present: this stop is for the structures he built, not for a visit he made.
stops.campa: Thirty-two years after the troops crossed, the army gives the island back to the province. What stands on it is what he left: the concrete cylinder, the shells of workshops, foundations of things begun and abandoned, a dock. It is the only monument he has, and it never worked for one verified minute. Mariscotti, who has walked the ground, reports that almost none of its constructions are habitable. The cypresses have come back up through the roads.
stops.quote: almost none of its constructions are habitable
stops.quote_source: Mario Mariscotti on the Huemul ruins, quoted in magicasruinas.com.ar, revista Esto, no. 287
suggested_refs: The ruins of the Huemul works, Lago Nahuel Huapi
Richter: Opera documental de camara (2003), music by Mario Lorenzo, libretto by Esteban Buch

stops.name: Monte Grande: dead on television
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the event, imprecise as to the day. Rionegro.com.ar records that at the beginning of September 1984 the television programme Alla vamos, on Canal 11, reported Richter as dead; no day is given and the first of the month orders the segment. The sightings that followed are recorded by the same source as rumour.
stops.campa: A television programme called Alla vamos announces on Canal 11 that Ronald Richter is dead. He is not. He is in Monte Grande with the shutters and the wife and the dogs, an hour from the studio. No correction is ever broadcast, and none of what follows is ever traced. When the error is exposed the country produces rumours instead: that he is alive but hidden at San Vicente near Peron's estate, that he has been seen in Washington, that he has been seen in Tel Aviv.
suggested_refs: The programme Alla vamos, Canal 11, early September 1984
sources: rionegro.com.ar, 'Richter, espias, Peron y la lealtad atomica'

stops.name: Monte Grande: the last interview
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the interview, over-precise as to the day. Elcordillerano.com.ar dates the visit only to around September 1984 and gives no day; rionegro.com.ar fixes the surrounding events to early September. The fifteenth is a convention used to order the segment and is not documented.
stops.campa: A journalist gets into the house. Richter is seventy-five, poor and entirely certain. He goes through it once more: the reaction happened, the plates were right, the commission was ignorant or bought, he returned the medal and the title. Then he leans toward the window and says there is someone on the slope of Cerro Otto watching him through binoculars. Cerro Otto stands above Bariloche, fifteen hundred kilometres to the southwest, and from its ridge you can see the island.
stops.quote: Hay alguien espiándome con largavistas desde la ladera del cerro Otto
stops.quote_source: Ronald Richter to the interviewer, Monte Grande, September 1984, elcordillerano.com.ar
suggested_refs: The 1984 interview, republished by elcordillerano.com.ar in January 2015
sources: rionegro.com.ar, 'Richter, espias, Peron y la lealtad atomica'
dataconurbano.net, 'Ronald Richter, un vecino de Monte Grande'

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the first of the two death dates
stops.date_confidence: contested. English Wikipedia gives 25 September 1991, citing a short notice in the obituary section of Microsemanario, and names no place; Buenos Aires here is inferred from his Monte Grande residence and is not documented. The competing tradition gives 29 December 1991 at Viedma. Neither is resolved and both are recorded in this file.
stops.campa: The older Argentine and English-language tradition has him dying on the twenty-fifth of September 1991. The evidence is a few lines in the obituary section of a university bulletin called Microsemanario. No place is named in it, and no cause. No burial is recorded in any source reached for this file, and no grave marked with his name has ever been located. A local historian who went looking around Monte Grande could not find a death certificate either.
suggested_refs: The Microsemanario obituary notice, 1991
sources: dataconurbano.net, 'Ronald Richter, un vecino de Monte Grande'

stops.name: Viedma: the second of the two death dates
stops.date_confidence: contested. Spanish and Czech Wikipedia give 29 December 1991 at Viedma, Rio Negro, at the age of 82, following recent Czech-derived sourcing; English Wikipedia gives 25 September 1991 with no place. Spanish Wikipedia is internally inconsistent, carrying both dates in one article. Neither language edition cites a primary document. Coordinates are those of Viedma.
stops.campa: The other tradition has him dying three months later and some nine hundred kilometres to the south, at Viedma on the Rio Negro, in the province that holds the lake and the island. He was eighty-two. The Czech and Spanish accounts carry this version; the English one keeps September and names no place at all, and the Spanish article carries both inside a single page. Argentina argued for forty years about whether the reaction of the sixteenth of February 1951 ever happened, and settled nothing. The two dates for his death cannot both be right. No certificate has been produced for either of them.
stops.quote: difficult to determine whether Richter was a clever impostor or a scientific nut
stops.quote_source: Juan G. Roederer, in the 2003 Physics Today exchange with Friedwardt Winterberg, quoted by ITER, 'Proyecto Huemul: the prank that started it all'
